This study used 18F-flortaucipir tau-PET (and amyloid PET) with structural MRI and FreeSurfer analyses, which does not satisfy I3. The paper does include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (20 patients) and healthy and AD comparison groups (I4, I5). It reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain comparisons (voxel-based SPM analyses), satisfying I7, but it does not fulfill the required imaging modality criterion; therefore it must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This is a single-case report (N=1) and does not meet the minimum sample size requirement (I5). The patient was clinically diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease and only had features consistent with bvFTD rather than being a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group, so I4 is not satisfied. Although the study used VBM and FDG-PET (I3) and reports whole-brain VBM results, the design is a case report rather than a group-level comparison of a bvFTD sample meeting the review’s sample-size and diagnostic requirements. Therefore it must be excluded.

The study does include a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=39) but does not use Voxel-Based Morphometry, fMRI, or FDG-PET. Imaging was based on visual rating scales of T1 MRI atrophy rather than voxelwise whole-brain analyses, and no MNI/Talairach coordinate-based between-group voxelwise results are reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports group-level voxelwise comparisons across bvFTD subgroups. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=80 after exclusions) and 30 healthy controls, satisfying sample size requirements. VBM analyses and voxelwise patterns (e.g., frontal and parietal atrophy differences across asymmetric and symmetric bvFTD) are described, and supplementary data are indicated, suggesting coordinate-based whole-brain results are available. No exclusion criteria are violated (not a review, not ROI-only, not an excluded modality). Therefore the study meets the review’s imaging, sample, and whole-brain reporting requirements.

This study includes VBM imaging and a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=11) with adequate sample sizes, but it does not report a whole-brain, between-group voxelwise contrast clearly attributable to the bvFTD group in MNI/Talairach space. The reported VBM results are regression associations of grey matter with behavioural measures across the combined patient cohort rather than group-level (bvFTD vs control or similar) whole-brain contrasts for the target group. Therefore the study fails to satisfy inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (reporting of a between-group, whole-brain voxelwise result for the target sample). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5. Exclusion criteria applicable: none of the listed explicit exclusion criteria; exclusion is due to failure to meet the required inclusion criteria (I6 and I7).

The study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=10) and adequate sample sizes (bvFTD N=10, HC N=18), so I4 and I5 are met. However, it does not use any of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET); instead it reports structural MRI FreeSurfer ROI volumetry and ROI-based analyses. The paper does not report whole-brain, voxelwise results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables, and there are no VBM or voxelwise group contrasts. Therefore it fails I3, I6, and I7. This qualifies as an exclusion under E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete for screening purposes (methods, results, discussion present).

This article is a narrative review of PET imaging applications across multiple CNS disorders and does not present original empirical data on behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). It does not report a sample of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, nor does it provide voxelwise, whole-brain group-level results or coordinate tables (MNI/Talairach) from VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET analyses. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria (no target sample, no empirical whole-brain imaging results). The paper is non-empirical review material and thus excluded under E5.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for structural analyses; includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=30); sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD n=30, AD n=25, controls n=25); reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain results with stereotactic coordinates (e.g., MNI coordinates reported for left frontoinsula and other clusters) and corrected statistics (pFWE and permutation thresholds). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses (masked to the salience network but using voxelwise thresholds and permutation correction) are clearly described in the text and results/tables. The full text provided includes introduction, methods (including MRI and VBM preprocessing), results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (systematic review, ROI-only, non-empirical, wrong imaging modality, or comorbid-psychiatric confounds) apply.

Although the paper includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=19) and adequate group sizes, it does not use VBM, fMRI (resting/task), or FDG-PET imaging and does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). Lesion maps are shown, but no voxelwise neuroimaging results or coordinate tables/contrasts are provided. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (no whole-brain results reported).

This is a single-case report (one symptomatic bvFTD proband) with neuropathologic comparisons to two other individuals; it does not meet the minimum sample size requirement (I5: at least 6 participants in patient or healthy group). Although the study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), and reports whole-brain VBM results (I7), it lacks a group-level patient sample and therefore cannot provide the group-level contrasts with adequate sample size required by the review. It is also unclear that VBM results are reported with stereotactic coordinates in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not satisfied). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that explicitly includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=17) alongside other FTD syndromes and healthy controls. Imaging modality is task fMRI with preprocessing and normalization into MNI space and second-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) SPM analyses reported (cluster- and peak-level results, figures/SPMs). Sample sizes satisfy the minimum (bvFTD group and control group ≥6). The paper provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results and displays SPMs and cluster/region findings in MNI space; figures and text clearly identify results for the bvFTD group. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and does not trigger exclusion criteria.

The study does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. It uses structural MRI with SIENA/SIENAX (not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), includes only a single bvFTD patient (n=1, below the required minimum of 6), and does not report any between-group voxelwise results in stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) coordinates or group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts. The full text appears complete but the methods and results do not provide the coordinate-based whole-brain findings required. Therefore it must be excluded.

This empirical study includes 14 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts reported in MNI space. Sample sizes (bvFTD n=14; controls n=28) exceed the minimum of 6. The paper provides whole-brain VBM results (group-level voxelwise analyses) and reports coordinates/figures; core article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the provided full text. Although the study also includes DTI analyses, it nevertheless meets the required imaging modality (VBM). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for this review.

This is an empirical study that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=23) and healthy controls, uses voxel-based morphometry and task-free (resting-state) fMRI as imaging modalities, reports whole-brain VBM voxelwise results with MNI coordinates, and presents group-level analyses relating structural and functional measures to autonomic outcomes. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6 per group). Whole-brain VBM results are reported and coordinates are provided (MNI), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise between-group/target-sample results. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, includes whole-brain analyses not only ROI, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria.

The study used voxel-based morphometry (SPM5) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (12 bvFTD among 20 right-temporal FTD subjects) and a control group (n=30), meeting the minimum sample size. Whole-brain VBM results (group-level contrasts) are presented and described; analyses were performed in standard stereotactic framework (SPM/MNI normalization). Therefore all imaging and reporting criteria for inclusion are met.

This is an empirical study of C9ORF72-associated FTD/ALS that includes clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD cases, but it does not meet the review's imaging and reporting requirements. Although FDG‑PET was performed, only five subjects had FDG‑PET (below the required N≥6). The MRI analysis used STAND-maps/region-based Z-scores rather than VBM and the paper does not report whole-brain, voxelwise between-group results in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) with coordinate tables for the target bvFTD sample. SPECT results included a voxelwise SPM analysis, but SPECT is not an accepted modality per I3. Therefore key inclusion criteria I3, I5, I6 and I7 are not satisfied.

The study does include clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients and adequate sample sizes, but it does not provide whole-brain, voxelwise neuroimaging results in a standard stereotactic space. Imaging reported consists of MRI visual rating scales and occasional FDG-PET in individuals without group-level voxelwise analyses or reported coordinates. Thus it fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (no whole-brain results). The full text appears complete.

Although the study is an empirical bvFTD study with sufficient sample size (14 bvFTD patients and 14 controls) and addresses ToM in clinically diagnosed bvFTD, it does not meet the imaging and whole-brain reporting requirements of the review. The imaging uses visual MRI ratings of prefrontal atrophy (qualitative/region-based scoring), not one of the required modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET; therefore I3 is not satisfied). The article provides no stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) coordinate results or group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses, and thus fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7. Per the review’s exclusion rules, this study reports no whole-brain voxelwise results (matches E3). Therefore it must be excluded despite meeting clinical/sample size criteria.

Although this full text reports voxelwise VBM and whole-brain resting-state fMRI results with MNI coordinates and adequate sample sizes, the participant group consists of presymptomatic C9ORF72 expansion carriers (preSxC9), not clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) patients. The meta-analysis requires studies including clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4). Therefore the study does not meet the key inclusion criterion I4 and must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This study meets the review objectives and inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to analyze grey matter (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (22 patients; I4, I5), and reports group-level voxelwise analyses aligned to MNI standard space (FNIRT to MNI152) with voxelwise results and cluster reports (I6). The paper provides group-level, voxelwise findings relating atrophy to behaviour (reported within a fronto‑subcortical mask but derived from voxelwise VBM analyses) and presents coordinates/clusters in figures/tables and supplementary materials, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting expectations (I7, I8). No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only without whole-brain results, non-empirical methods) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical VBM study reporting whole-brain voxelwise analyses in clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients. The sample includes 18 bvFTD patients (14 entered MRI/VBM) and 36 controls (20 imaged), meeting the minimum group sizes. The paper reports between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs HC) and voxelwise correlation analyses using SPM/VBM with cluster-level FWE correction, providing group-level whole-brain results attributed to the target sample. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and not using only excluded modalities).

Although this study includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=27) and meets sample-size and reporting requirements (voxel-wise whole-brain TBSS results reported in groupwise/MNI space), the imaging modality used is diffusion tensor imaging (DTI). The review’s inclusion requires VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and the exclusion criteria explicitly disallow studies that only report DTI (E6). Therefore the study must be excluded despite satisfying other inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=55) and used FDG-PET in a subset, it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses or between-group contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI or Talairach) with coordinates. Imaging was rated qualitatively by experts rather than analyzed voxelwise; no tables/figures of voxelwise coordinates or whole-brain statistical maps are provided. Therefore it fails the required inclusion criteria for reporting between-group, whole-brain results (I6, I7) despite meeting I3, I4, and I5. Excluded on that basis.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses FDG-PET imaging (I3), includes clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (N=82) (I4) with matched healthy controls and subgroup sizes ≥6 (I5). The methods describe whole-brain, voxel-wise SPM analyses producing group-level t-maps and between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs HC and variant comparisons), reported with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level corrections, indicating results in standard stereotactic space (SPM/MNI) (I6, I7). Whole-brain voxelwise resting-state metabolic connectivity (IRCA) and SICE results are reported and discussed; coordinate/table/figure reporting is implied/standard for SPM results (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not limited to disallowed modalities, and comorbid AD was assessed/excluded). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study meets the review criteria: it uses whole-brain Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) analyses (methods and voxelwise regression reported), includes a diagnostically defined bvFTD patient sample (20 patients, including genetically confirmed cases and probable bvFTD), and has adequate sample sizes (20 patients, 20 controls). The paper reports group-level voxelwise results and provides MNI coordinates for voxelwise findings (e.g., IFG peak at MNI −41, 26, 3) from whole-brain analyses. A two-sample VBM group comparison (patients vs. controls) is described as a voxelwise, whole-brain analysis. Supplementary materials are referenced for additional tables/coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not ROI-only; imaging modality acceptable). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality, includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=19), has sample sizes >6, reports voxelwise whole-brain results with MNI coordinates, and provides group-level whole-brain covariate analyses (FWE/FDR-corrected) clearly attributed to the bvFTD sample. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (VBM procedures), Results (tables/figures with MNI coordinates), and Discussion, so the full text is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not a review, not ROI-only, not an excluded imaging modality, and no evidence of disqualifying comorbidities).

This empirical study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality, includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=25), and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts and correlations with stereotactic coordinates (MNI) for bvFTD vs controls and behaviour–brain associations. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD n=25; controls n=25). The full text contains Introduction, Methods (including MRI acquisition and VBM preprocessing/analysis), Results (group VBM comparisons and covariate analyses), and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are violated (not a review, not ROI-only, and participant exclusions for comorbid psychiatric/other dementias/substance abuse were applied). Therefore the paper provides whole-brain VBM results from a bvFTD cohort suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) alongside DTI, includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=12), and provides whole-brain, voxelwise between-group analyses registered to MNI space with results corrected for multiple comparisons. Sample sizes meet the minimum (≥6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain VBM results and voxelwise contrasts (figures/tables and text), satisfying the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are violated.

This is a single-case clinical report describing one patient with probable behavioral-variant FTD and includes an FDG-PET scan. Although it meets I3 (uses FDG-PET) and I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD), it does not meet required sample- or analysis-related inclusion criteria: the study has n=1 (fails I5), presents no between-group contrasts or coordinate-based results in MNI/Talairach space (fails I6), and reports no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from the target sample (fails I7). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it must be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on group-level neuroimaging studies.

This is an original empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=49) and healthy controls (n=30) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts and regression analyses. The methods explicitly use voxel-based morphometry with whole-brain thresholds and report peak voxel coordinates (converted to Talairach), and results are presented in figures/tables relating GM density to self-appraisal measures. The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion. Thus it satisfies imaging modality (VBM), target diagnosis (bvFTD), adequate sample size, whole-brain voxelwise results in a standard stereotactic space, and acceptable reporting formats.

The full text reports clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=27) and includes resting-state fMRI (ICA dual-regression) analyses, meeting the imaging modality requirement. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts were performed and results are reported/visualized in MNI standard space (TBSS and dual-regression RS-fMRI results), satisfying coordinate and whole-brain evidence requirements. Sample sizes (bvFTD=27; controls=48) exceed the minimum. Results are presented in figures/tables and supplementary materials. The full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete.

Although this paper uses FDG-PET (I3) and studies clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with 12 healthy controls (satisfying I5 via the healthy group), it does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The analyses are ROI-based CMRGlc comparisons and visual MRI ratings without voxelwise, whole-brain coordinate results (fails I6 and I7). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

The study is an empirical VBM investigation of behavioural variant FTD including genetically defined subgroups and a sporadic bvFTD comparison. It uses voxel-based morphometry (I3) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD groups to controls and between disease groups (I7,I8). The sample size exceeds the minimum (multiple patient groups >6 and controls n=40) (I5), and participants were clinically diagnosed with behavioural variant FTD (I4). The methods use SPM5 normalization and report voxelwise results (VBM) that would be in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) and are presented in figures/tables, satisfying the requirement for reporting between-group contrasts in a defined space (I6). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext is complete.

This study meets the review objective and key imaging/participant criteria: it performed whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses and reports stereotactic coordinates (x,y,z = -24,-14,14) for a significant cluster in the left putamen. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=16) and adequate comparison groups (AD n=14, HC n=20). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results from the target sample (FTD) are reported and neuroimaging analyses are thresholded (p<0.05 FWE) with cluster size reported. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and neuroimaging details, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review only, ROI-only analysis, disallowed modalities, comorbid psychiatric sample) apply.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses FDG-PET imaging (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=26) (I4) with sufficient sample size (I5), and performs voxel-based, whole-brain SPM analyses with images spatially normalized to MNI space and reports voxelwise between-group contrasts and correlations (I6,I7). Results are reported in figures and supplementary tables (I8). No exclusion criteria apply: this is an empirical FDG-PET voxelwise study (not a review or ROI-only), and the sample selection excluded comorbid psychiatric/other dementia cases. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study does include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=19) and adequate sample size, but it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements. The imaging approach is manual hypothalamic volumetry on structural MRI (ROI-based), not VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not satisfied). The paper reports regional volume comparisons and correlations rather than any between-group voxelwise results in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) and therefore does not provide whole-brain, coordinate-based contrasts (I6 and I7 not satisfied). This constitutes an ROI-only analysis, which falls under exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4) and adequate sample sizes (I5), it does not use an eligible imaging modality (I3). Imaging consists of structural MRI volumetric analyses using FreeSurfer (regional/ROI volumes and cortical volumetry), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. The paper reports ROI-based volumetric results rather than any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results or stereotactic coordinates (fails I6 and I7). Therefore it reports only ROI/volume analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise findings and is excluded under E3 and E6.

The study does not use the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET); it reports T1-weighted MRI volumetric (whole thalamus) ROI analyses rather than voxelwise whole-brain results in stereotactic space. Although it includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=141) and adequate sample sizes, it provides no between-group voxelwise coordinates (MNI/Talairach) or whole-brain voxelwise results. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7.

This is a single-case report (n=1) with FDG-PET and MRI imaging of one patient diagnosed with bvFTD due to C9orf72 expansion. Although imaging modality criterion (I3) and presence of clinically diagnosed bvFTD (I4) are satisfied, the study fails key required inclusion criteria: it does not meet the minimum sample size (I5: <6 participants), does not report any between-group contrasts or results in a standard stereotactic space (I6), and provides no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (I7). Therefore it does not provide the group-level whole-brain coordinate data needed for the meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This is an original empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=15) with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results and reported peak coordinates. It includes a healthy control group (n=20). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and reports between-group contrasts (disease vs controls and between pathologies) with tables of peak voxel coordinates. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

The study is a VBM whole-brain group analysis and reports MNI coordinates, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, and has adequate sample sizes (10 patient carriers, 20 sporadic FTD, 20 controls). However, the patient sample includes individuals with concurrent neurological/psychiatric conditions (one with ALS, two with parkinsonian signs, one with psychotic symptoms, one with Paget’s disease), which violates the review exclusion criterion E4 that excludes samples with other neurological or psychiatric comorbidities. Therefore the study must be excluded despite meeting the imaging/reporting criteria.

This is an empirical neuropsychological study of episodic memory in bvFTD and AD that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and adequate sample sizes. However, it does not use any of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) and does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 and cannot be included in the imaging-focused meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Although this study used VBM (I3), included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), and had adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n=12; controls n=17) meeting the N>=6 requirement (I5), it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts (e.g., bvFTD vs. controls) in MNI/Talairach space. The imaging analyses are voxelwise correlational analyses of grey-matter volume with flavour/odour identification across an FTLD cohort, with a restricted bvFTD subgroup analysis reported only at a relaxed uncorrected threshold; no standard group-level between-group contrast coordinates or whole-brain group comparison results originating from the bvFTD group are presented. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 (at least one between-group contrast in defined stereotactic space) and I7 (reporting at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result clearly from the target sample group) are not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

This is a clinical/epidemiological study of epilepsy in neurodegenerative dementias using clinical assessment, EEG/qEEG and routine MRI for diagnosis. Although the sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and the bvFTD group size exceeds 6 (I5), the study does not use VBM, task/resting‑state fMRI, or FDG‑PET as an imaging modality (fails I3). It does not report any whole‑brain, voxelwise between‑group contrasts in stereotactic space or provide coordinate tables/voxelwise results (fails I6 and I7). Therefore it does not meet required imaging and reporting criteria for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study uses VBM and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=22), and reports voxelwise results with MNI coordinates. However, the VBM analyses and reported whole-brain voxelwise results are presented for the combined FTLD cohort (and separately for AD) or as correlations with symptoms, not as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts clearly identified as coming specifically from the bvFTD subgroup (the target sample). Therefore inclusion criterion I7 (at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the target sample group) is not met. Full text appears complete.

This is a single-family case series/report. Although the study used FDG-PET (satisfying I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases (satisfying I4), it does not meet key inclusion criteria: sample size is well below the required minimum of 6 participants in a patient or healthy group (I5 not met), and no between-group voxelwise contrasts in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables are reported (I6 and I7 not met). The imaging findings are presented as individual case images and descriptive observations rather than whole-brain, group-level statistical maps or coordinate tables. Therefore it must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This randomized crossover study includes task and resting fMRI (I3), clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4), and sufficient sample size (28 participants; I5). However, imaging results were reported as non-significant and the manuscript states ‘data not shown’; no between-group (patient vs control) whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported, and no coordinates in MNI or Talairach space are provided. Thus the study does not meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (no between-group stereotactic coordinates and no reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). Because no whole-brain coordinate results are available for the target patient group, it cannot be included in a coordinate-based meta-analysis and should be excluded (applies to exclusion criterion E3).

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as an imaging modality, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=15), has sufficient group sizes (bvFTD and controls >6), reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts registered to MNI standard space (methods describe MNI registration and results are displayed/overlayed on MNI templates), and provides group-level whole-brain results (VBM/TBSS) clearly attributed to the bvFTD sample. The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion (not truncated). There are no applicable exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, non-empirical, seed-FC/DTI-only) that would disqualify the paper. Therefore it should be included for the meta-analysis focusing on bvFTD VBM studies.

This study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD sample per Rascovsky criteria (I4) with 52 patients (I5). Voxel-wise SPM analyses were performed, including single-subject SPM maps and group-level whole-brain two-sample t-tests against a normal FDG-PET database, producing voxelwise (SPM/MNI-based) results and conjunction analyses (I6, I7). Results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise maps and described in the text/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, non-empirical, wrong imaging modality, or comorbid psychiatric/other dementia confounds) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

Although this study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=36) and meets the sample-size requirement, it does not use any of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). The imaging reported is structural MRI/CT and PET/SPECT analyzed by visual reads rather than voxelwise FDG-PET analyses. The paper does not report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise results in a standard stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach) or provide coordinate tables. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

Although the study is a full empirical resting-state fMRI investigation including clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, adequate sample sizes, voxelwise whole-brain seed-based analyses normalized to MNI space, and reports group-level between-group contrasts, it reports only seed-based functional connectivity (wSDM and Pearson correlation) results from resting-state fMRI. Per exclusion criterion E6, studies that only report seed-based functional connectivity (FC) without other accepted modalities (e.g., VBM or FDG-PET) are excluded from this review. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Hence the paper must be excluded despite meeting multiple inclusion elements.

The full text reports voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) whole-brain analyses linking DEXA-derived body-composition measures to grey-matter atrophy in a clearly defined bvFTD sample. The study includes 28 bvFTD patients (meets sample size requirement), reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level results (voxelwise P<0.005, cluster extent threshold provided) with anatomical labeling in stereotactic space (MNI), and presents figures/tables of these results. The full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion sections, sufficient for screening.

The study reports empirical VBM analyses including bvFTD patients and healthy controls, with whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons and ROI analyses. Sample sizes meet the minimum (bvFTD n=23; controls n=50). Imaging data were normalized to MNI space and SPM-based voxelwise results are reported for between-group contrasts. The full text includes introduction, methods (VBM acquisition and analysis), results (whole-brain and insula ROI findings), and discussion, allowing assessment against inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=11) and uses resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM). The methods state that voxelwise analyses were performed with x–y–z coordinates in Montreal Neurological Institute space, and VBM produced whole-brain, voxelwise atrophy results for the bvFTD group (P<0.05, FDR-corrected). Sample sizes meet the minimum (≥6). Whole-brain voxelwise group-level results are reported (main text and supplemental material referenced). No exclusion criteria are met: this is empirical original data (not a review), it is not limited to only ROI or seed-based FC analyses (VBM whole-brain results present), and there is no indication of comorbid psychiatric disorders or other excluded features. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion); supplemental materials are available. Therefore the study meets all specified inclusion criteria for the review.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bv-FTD patients (n=27) (I4), has sufficient sample size (≥6) (I5), reports voxelwise results in MNI space with peak coordinates (I6), and provides whole-brain, group-level VBM results (cluster surviving FWE correction) clearly identified as coming from the patient groups (I7,I8). The full text contains introduction, methods (including imaging and VBM preprocessing/statistics), results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (study is empirical, not ROI-only, uses acceptable imaging modality, and does not appear to be a review or non-empirical paper).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) methods on T1-weighted MRI (ICA on modulated gray matter images and voxel-wise VBM analyses), includes clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (n=24), has adequate sample size (bvFTD n=24; AD n=31; controls n=30), reports between-group contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results in MNI space (voxel-wise permutation testing, TFCE, FWE-corrected; SCN clusters listed with MNI coordinates), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise findings attributable to the bvFTD group. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and uses whole-brain VBM (with N>6 bvFTD cases) and reports voxelwise results in MNI space, it does not report any between-group contrasts (e.g., patient group vs. controls) nor any bvFTD-specific group-level whole-brain voxelwise results. The primary VBM analyses are across a mixed patient cohort using regression with insight scores; subgroup analyses by diagnostic group produced no significant results. Therefore the study fails to meet I6 (between-group contrast reported in defined stereotactic space) and I7 (at least one group-level whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from the target sample group). Full text appears complete.

The study reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients to healthy controls, with adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n=20, HC n=20). Results are reported in MNI space with voxelwise between-group contrasts and cluster coordinates, and whole-brain conjunction analyses are presented. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets the review’s imaging modality, sample, sample size, reporting of between-group contrasts in standard space, and whole-brain result requirements.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (36 bvFTD + 20 FTD-ALS) and healthy controls (n=23). The study used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM), reports group atrophy contrasts and voxelwise correlations with psychosis scores, and provides anatomical coordinates in MNI stereotaxic space (results in main text and supplementary tables). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6 per group). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results from the target bvFTD sample are clearly reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses, reviews, disallowed modalities) are violated.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses FDG-PET imaging (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with adequate sample size (8 bvFTD patients and 26 controls; I5), reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with peak coordinates (Table III) in stereotactic space (I6), and provides group-level, whole-brain results clearly identified for the target sample (I7). Reporting of results in tables/figures/text satisfies I8. No exclusion criteria are violated (not a review, not ROI-only, not using excluded modalities, and comorbid diagnoses were excluded). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete.

This is a DTI study using ROI analyses (FWM, GWM, SWM) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and it does not report whole-brain voxelwise results or stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach). Although it includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=8) and sufficient sample sizes, it violates the imaging-modality requirement and reports only ROI-based DTI results, which are excluded by the review criteria.

The study meets several inclusion criteria (FDG-PET imaging, clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample, adequate sample size, and reports voxelwise MNI coordinates), but it does not report a between-group contrast (e.g., patients vs. controls). Instead, the paper presents within-group voxelwise regression analyses relating occupational scores to rCMRglc. Inclusion criterion I6 explicitly requires at least one between-group contrast reported in defined stereotactic space; this is not present, so the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This empirical study used FDG-PET and VBM (voxel-based morphometry) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM results (including MNI coordinates) comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=24) to controls (n=12). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (patients and controls). The paper presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (SPM VBM analysis) with coordinates and statistical maps, and provides ROI and voxelwise PET analyses. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; does not restrict to ROI-only analyses; excludes comorbid psychiatric/substance cases). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8.

This is a genetic case-family report of FTDP-17 with imaging of individual family members (MRI, FDG-PET) but it does not meet key inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis. The study sample is small (≤5 siblings, only 2–3 affected)—failing I5 (minimum N=6). It does not present any group-level, between-group voxelwise contrasts or whole-brain results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach), failing I6 and I7. Although FDG-PET was used (satisfying I3), the data are reported as single cases/family imaging and not as whole-brain group analyses. Therefore it cannot be included in a voxelwise meta-analysis of bvFTD studies.

This is an empirical, longitudinal resting-state fMRI study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=12) and control/AD groups (controls n=22, AD n=20), meeting sample size requirements. Imaging modality is resting-state fMRI (satisfies I3). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise network-to-region analyses using registration to MNI space and nonparametric permutation testing (FSL-randomize), with group-level voxelwise results and post hoc contrasts described across baseline and follow-up (satisfies I6, I7, I8). The study provides voxel-based morphometry analyses as well and corrects functional results for gray matter volume. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, includes whole-brain results, not seed-only, and participants were screened for major psychiatric/other neurologic comorbidities). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

Although the study uses resting-state fMRI (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=38) (I4), and has adequate sample sizes (I5), it reports ROI-based graph/network analyses and network-based statistics (NBS) on a 220-node parcellation rather than whole-brain voxelwise contrasts with stereotactic coordinates. The manuscript does not present group-level, voxelwise results in MNI/Talairach space or coordinate tables required by I6/I7. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/network analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical FDG-PET study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=42) and healthy controls, with voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses comparing bvFTD versus controls and apathetic versus non-apathetic subgroups. Imaging was normalized to a standard space and results are reported as voxelwise clusters (with tables of cluster locations referenced). Sample sizes exceed the minimum threshold. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=10), uses voxelwise morphometry-like methods and structural MRI, and has adequate sample sizes, it does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) results clearly identified for the bvFTD group. The voxelwise morphometry was restricted to a merged subcortical mask (not whole-brain), and cortical thickness (whole-brain) results for bvFTD did not reach significance and no whole-brain coordinate-based results for bvFTD are provided in the text. The paper therefore lacks the required whole-brain, voxelwise between-group results in standard stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach) for the target sample. Based on the review criteria, this study must be excluded.

The study does include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=9) but does NOT use any of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET); it uses 18F‑THK5351 tau PET (a different PET tracer) and 18F‑florbetaben amyloid PET. Primary analyses are region-of-interest (lobe-based SUVR/WM/GM ratios) rather than whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. The paper does not report voxelwise, whole-brain group-level contrasts or coordinate tables that satisfy the whole‑brain/voxelwise requirement. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This full text meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (50 bvFTD subjects) within the sample (I4); sample sizes exceed the minimum (I5); reports voxelwise, between-group contrasts with Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) coordinates (I6); provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results clearly identified for FTD and bvFTD (I7); and coordinate results/figures/tables are reported in the text/supplement (I8). The article contains complete core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusions) and does not violate exclusion criteria. Therefore it should be included.

The paper is an empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as its imaging modality, included 19 clinically probable bvFTD patients (and control/disease groups), and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results with coordinates provided in MNI stereotaxic space. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only analyses, disallowed imaging modalities, or comorbid samples) are violated. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

While the paper uses FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases (I4), and compares scans to a large healthy control dataset (N=112) satisfying the sample-size requirement for a control group (I5), it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) result derived from the bvFTD target sample. The study reports single-subject SPM voxelwise maps rather than a group-level voxelwise contrast for the bvFTD subgroup (bvFTD n=2), so it fails inclusion criterion I7. The presented results are single-subject voxelwise maps/figures (acceptable per I8) but do not meet the review requirement of at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result for the target clinical group. Full text appears complete.

The study uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with FSL-VBM and reports voxel-wise results referenced to MNI space. It includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) and healthy controls, with sample sizes above the minimum threshold. The paper provides whole-brain group-level contrasts and covariate VBM analyses, reports anatomical locations and states MNI stereotaxic coordinates, and describes overlap/exclusive masking results (tables/figures/supplementary). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses, reviews, disallowed modalities, or comorbid diagnostic confounds) are met.

This is a clinical case series of eight Chinese individuals with FTD describing clinical, neuropsychological, and some structural MRI and PIB amyloid PET findings. It does not use voxel-based morphometry (VBM), FDG-PET, or task/resting-state fMRI as the imaging modality (fails I3). The paper does not report any between-group voxelwise whole-brain contrasts in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) nor provide coordinate-based results (fails I6 and I7). Although it includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (satisfies I4) and the sample size meets the ≥6 participants criterion (satisfies I5), the lack of the required imaging modality and absence of whole-brain voxelwise results make it ineligible for inclusion.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It uses SPECT (rCBF) rather than permitted imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) (fails I3). It also does not report between-group contrasts vs. a healthy/control group in a defined stereotactic space (fails I6), reporting only within-group voxelwise correlations. Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), has sufficient sample size (I5), and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI coordinates (I7, I8), failure to meet I3 and I6 means it must be excluded per the review’s criteria.

The study uses structural MRI volumetry and surface-based cortical thickness analyses (FreeSurfer), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET required by I3. This falls under exclusion E6 (studies reporting only cortical thickness methods). Although the sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and has >=6 healthy controls (I5), the imaging modality does not meet inclusion criteria for the review. Whole-brain vertex-wise thickness results are reported but are surface-based cortical measures rather than the required modalities and do not clearly provide stereotactic coordinate tables in MNI/Talairach for bvFTD-specific contrasts, so the study cannot be included.

This study used voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) and reported whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts (density analyses) including a group of patients meeting criteria for behavioral variant FTD comorbid with ALS (ALS-FTD; n=7). Healthy controls (n=39) and the patient subgroup sizes meet the minimum sample size criterion. The paper presents whole-brain VBM results and ROI density analyses with figures and supplementary tables referenced, indicating voxelwise between-group contrasts attributable to the target bvFTD group. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not alternative modality). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

Although this empirical study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=19) and uses FDG-PET (satisfying I3, I4, I5), it does not report a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD sample (I7) nor provide between-group voxelwise contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (I6). The voxel-based analyses described are correlational across the pooled sample (with diagnostic group as a covariate) and ROI analyses are reported for frontal regions; coordinate tables or voxelwise between-group contrasts for the bvFTD group are not presented in the provided full text (coordinates are referenced as Supplementary Table S2 but no bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise coordinates/contrasts are shown). Therefore it fails required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This empirical study reports voxel-wise gray matter density (T1 MRI) analyses comparing 32 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients to 17 healthy controls using whole-brain voxel-wise methods (Randomise with family-wise error correction). Sample sizes exceed the minimum. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain contrast results and regression of f0 range with GM atrophy, with peak voxels summarized in table e-1 (supplementary), satisfying reporting of results in a defined stereotactic space. There is no evidence of excluded sample comorbidities or disqualifying methods. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary peak coordinates are referenced. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for VBM-style whole-brain analysis in bvFTD.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=11), uses VBM, and has adequate group sizes, the imaging results reported are region-of-interest volumetric comparisons (hippocampus and posterior cingulate) rather than whole-brain voxelwise group-level contrasts reported in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) with coordinates. The manuscript does not present voxelwise whole-brain results or coordinate tables/figures for between-group contrasts. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I7) and falls under exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

The study reports primary empirical data using baseline structural T1 MRI processed into voxel-wise grey-matter maps (CAT12/DARTEL) consistent with VBM-style analysis and whole-brain voxel-wise features (I3). The sample includes clinically diagnosed probable/definite bvFTD patients (n=18) based on FTDC criteria at 2-year follow-up (I4), and group sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD n=18; psychiatric n=27; neurological n=28) (I5). Images were normalized to MNI space and the paper presents multivariate, whole-brain voxelwise results (SVM weight maps with p-values) with anatomical localization reported in the main text and supplementary materials (Supplementary Table 5, Fig.2), which satisfies reporting of results in a defined stereotactic space and whole-brain group-level voxelwise evidence (I6, I7, I8). The study is empirical, not a review, and includes whole-brain analyses (no exclusion criteria triggered). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion); supplementary material is referenced. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for this review.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry and resting-state fMRI (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12) compared with healthy controls (I4,I5), and reports group-level whole-brain analyses using SPM with normalization to MNI space and VBM comparisons (I6,I7). The manuscript describes voxelwise VBM results and ICA-derived resting-state network analyses, and indicates supplementary materials with brain regions/networks (acceptable per I8). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext considered complete). No exclusion criteria (e.g., review only, ROI-only, seed-only FC, DTI-only, or comorbid-sample issues) are triggered based on the provided content.

This is an empirical resting-state fMRI study using ICA-derived intrinsic connectivity networks, including a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) and matched controls and AD patients. The study uses task-free fMRI (meets I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4) with sufficient sample size per group (n=12; I5), reports voxel-wise, whole-brain group contrasts with peak coordinates (MNI) and corrected thresholds (I6, I7), and presents results in figures/tables/text (I8). Full article text including methods, results, and discussion is provided. No exclusion criteria (reviews, ROI-only, seed-only/DTI/cortical thickness, non-empirical design) apply.

The study includes voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (methods and results described), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12) and controls (n=20), and reports group-level voxelwise between-group contrasts using SPM/DARTEL with images normalized to MNI space and cluster-based FWE correction. Whole-brain VBM results (gray matter loss in specific regions) are reported and clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets imaging modality (I3), bvFTD sample (I4), sufficient sample size (I5), between-group voxelwise results in stereotactic space (I6), and whole-brain group-level voxelwise reporting (I7/I8). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical FDG-PET study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (final n=21) with age- and education-matched controls. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses using MNI space coordinates and FWE-corrected results (e.g., dmPFC and right amygdala), and parametric within-group regression analyses linking regional hypometabolism to prosocial and other-critical sentiment scores. Imaging modality (FDG-PET), sample (clinically diagnosed bvFTD), sample size (>6 per group), and reporting of between-group and group-level whole-brain voxelwise results in stereotactic space meet the inclusion criteria. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only, non-empirical methods, or disallowed modalities) are met.

This study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with SPM8 (I3), included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (18 bvFTD patients) (I4) and healthy controls with group sizes >6 (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons (controls > FTD) and voxelwise correlations between EDS scores and grey matter density (group-level, whole-brain results) using standard VBM preprocessing/normalization (SPM template space) and reports regional results in tables/figures (I6, I7, I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only analysis, disallowed modalities, or comorbid sample issues) are met. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the review.

Although this study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=14) and uses resting-state fMRI (satisfying I3, I4, I5), the analyses are ROI/seed-based functional connectivity measures and the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast results with coordinates in standard stereotactic space. The meta-analysis requires at least one whole-brain voxelwise result (I6/I7). Therefore the study is excluded because it reports only ROI/seed-based analyses (E3, E6). Full text appears complete.

The article uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (and FDG-PET) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients. Although the main focus is two bvFTD-SP case patients, the paper also generated group-level whole-brain VBM maps comparing 20 bvFTD patients to 164 controls (voxelwise, p<0.001) for comparative purposes. Sample sizes therefore meet the >=6 participant requirement (20 bvFTD; 164 controls). Whole-brain voxelwise results are presented as VBM maps (figures) with MNI-referenced template coordinates described in the text/figure legend, satisfying the requirement for between-group contrasts in a defined stochastic space and acceptable reporting via figures. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is a case report of two relatives (n=1 patient of interest and neuropathology from his father). Although FDG-PET was performed (I3) and the diagnoses are frontal-variant FTD (consistent with bvFTD; I4), the study does not meet key inclusion requirements: sample size is far below the required minimum (I5), no voxelwise whole-brain analyses or reported coordinates are provided (I6/I7/I8), and results are descriptive rather than reported in a defined stereotactic space. The paper is therefore not eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The paper reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=13) (I4). Sample sizes meet the threshold (I5). VBM results are reported as voxelwise, whole-brain contrasts with coordinates in stereotaxic space (MNI) (I6, I7), and results are presented in figures/tables described in text (I8). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

Although the sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=18) and adequate sample size, the study uses structural MRI cortical thickness ROI analyses (FreeSurfer) rather than VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET, and it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise results in a standard stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach) or provide coordinate tables. Therefore it fails key imaging and whole-brain reporting inclusion criteria (I3, I6, I7). This qualifies it for exclusion under E3 (ROI-only analyses without whole-brain results) and E6 (reports cortical thickness methods rather than allowed modalities). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=66) with age- and gender-matched controls (n=30). The paper uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons of each bvFTD-derived subtype versus controls (family-wise error corrected; additional pairwise contrasts reported). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). Whole-brain results are described in the text and shown in figures (and referred to in tables), meeting the requirement for voxelwise between-group results in stereotactic space. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so core content is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review, only ROI analyses, seed-based FC/DTI-only methods) apply.

This study reports empirical voxel-wise FDG-PET analyses comparing behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) patients (n=12) with AD and control groups. It uses FDG-PET as an imaging modality, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants, has more than six patients in the bvFTD group, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results in MNI space with reported coordinates and statistical maps. The manuscript contains full introduction, methods, results, and discussion sections. There are no exclusion criteria triggered (not a review, not ROI-only, not a non-empirical methods paper, and not limited to excluded modalities). Therefore it meets all specified inclusion criteria for the review.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses FDG-PET (and VBM) as imaging modalities (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients confirmed after 12-month follow-up (I4), has adequate sample sizes (30 patients, 42 controls) exceeding the 6-participant threshold (I5), and reports voxel-wise, whole-brain analyses normalized to a stereotactic space (images were normalized to MNI space using SPM8 with voxel-based DTI and VBM results), satisfying the requirement for between-group contrasts in defined stochastic space (I6) and providing group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (I7). Results are presented in figures and described in text (acceptable per I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=22), uses VBM, and has adequate sample sizes. However, the VBM analysis yielded no significant whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results (no findings surviving whole-brain FWE correction); significant effects were reported only after small-volume (ROI) correction. The review exclusion criterion E3 disallows studies that report only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results. Therefore the study does not meet the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise results (I7/I6) and must be excluded.

Although the study uses FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), and has sufficient sample size (I5), it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI or Talairach). The paper presents diagnostic accuracy, individual example images and qualitative readings, but no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. The study should be excluded from the meta-analysis that requires voxelwise, coordinate-based whole-brain results.

Although the study includes bvFTD patients and used [18F]FDG‑PET and MRI (satisfying I3, I4, I5), the imaging data were assessed by visual rating and categorized as presence/absence of frontotemporal abnormalities. The paper does not report any voxelwise, whole‑brain group comparisons nor provide stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) or VBM/fMRI/FDG‑PET statistical maps. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 and provides no whole‑brain voxelwise results. Exclusion criterion E3 (no whole‑brain results / only non‑voxelwise visual/qualitative imaging) applies. Full text appears complete.

This full text clearly meets all required inclusion criteria: the study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality; includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=23); samples sizes exceed the minimum (patient groups and controls >=16); analyses were registered to MNI152 standard space and report voxelwise, group-level contrasts (voxelwise GLM with TFCE, permutation testing) and results are overlaid on the MNI standard brain; whole-brain voxelwise results are presented for patient vs control and inter-patient contrasts and for clinical correlations. The manuscript contains full methods, results and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria (reviews, ROI-only results, unsupported modalities, or non-empirical design) appear to apply.

This study does not meet the imaging- and sample-specific inclusion criteria for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis. Although it is an empirical study with adequate sample sizes (93 mutation carriers, 78 noncarriers) and reports longitudinal structural MRI analyses, the participants are familial FTLD mutation carriers (many presymptomatic or mildly/questionably symptomatic) rather than a cohort of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients. The imaging analyses reported are lobar ROI-based gray matter volumes/atrophy associations (summed atlas regions) rather than voxelwise VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET whole-brain contrasts in standard stereotactic space. The paper does not report between-group whole-brain voxelwise coordinate results in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails I3, I4, I6, and I7. It does meet sample size criterion I5. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) as the imaging modality and reports voxelwise, group-level results (including cluster coordinates) aligned to MNI space. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=30), satisfying the requirement for bvFTD inclusion and the minimum sample size (>=6). Whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts and correlation analyses are clearly reported in the main text and figures/tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not just abstract/metadata), and no exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only analyses) apply. Consequently the paper should be INCLUDED.

The study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses relating caregiver-rated empathy measures to gray-matter atrophy in a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup. The methods describe whole-brain VBM in SPM99 with group-level contrasts comparing bvFTD (N=12) to healthy controls and regression analyses linking IRI subscales to gray-matter atrophy; results include cluster-level findings and a table of VBM results. Sample sizes meet the threshold (bvFTD N=12; controls N=16). The paper provides whole-brain, voxelwise group results derived from the target bvFTD group and reports coordinates/clusters (Table 2, Figure 1). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this study uses VBM and FDG-PET and reports voxel-wise, MNI-space group contrasts, it does not specifically address behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) as the target sample. The patient sample is familial FTLD with mixed clinical phenotypes (bvFTD, nfvPPA, PSP, ALS), and the paper presents whole-brain results for f-FTLD subgroups (A+ vs A−) rather than a group clearly and explicitly defined as clinically diagnosed bvFTD. It is unclear how many (if any) bvFTD cases are present and whether there are ≥6 bvFTD patients; no group-level, whole-brain results are reported specifically for a bvFTD sample. Therefore the key inclusion criterion I4 (bvFTD sample) and I7 (whole-brain results clearly from target bvFTD group) are not satisfied, so the study must be excluded.

The full text reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses using FSL (MNI standard space) and provides group-level, voxelwise contrasts (including MNI coordinates and figures/tables) comparing bvFTD patients to controls. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=44) and controls (n=28), satisfying the sample size requirement. Imaging modality (VBM), presence of clinically diagnosed bvFTD, ≥6 participants, reporting of between-group contrasts in MNI space, and whole-brain voxelwise group results are all present. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria are violated.

Although this is a longitudinal MRI study including clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=37) and sufficient sample size, the imaging modality and analysis used (surface-based cortical thickness via FreeSurfer and subcortical volumetry) do not match the meta-analysis inclusion requirement of VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. The protocol explicitly excludes studies that report only cortical thickness methods. While the paper reports whole-brain vertex-wise surface analyses and between-group contrasts, the primary imaging measure is cortical thickness (surface-based), triggering exclusion under E6.

This empirical study uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (FSL–VBM) to examine neural correlates in behavior variant FTD (bvFTD) and Alzheimer’s groups. The sample includes 10 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (and 10 AD, 10 controls), satisfying sample-size requirements. VBM analyses report voxelwise, group-level results and brain–behavior correlations with coordinates provided in MNI stereotaxic space. The full text includes introduction, methods (image acquisition and VBM), results (group atrophy maps, voxelwise correlates), and discussion. No exclusion criteria are triggered: it is not a review, not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/DTI/thickness-only methods, and participants with comorbid psychiatric/neurological conditions or substance abuse were excluded per the Methods. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical FDG-PET study (SPM12) that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=24) and healthy controls. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (t-statistic maps normalized to MNI space) and between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls; bvFTD vs AD) with cluster-level FWE correction, and presents anatomo–functional correlations. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). Whole-brain results are explicitly described in the methods and results (MNI space), satisfying the requirement for reported between-group contrasts in a defined stochastic space. No exclusion criteria appear to be violated. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical study with clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=11) and early-onset AD (n=14). It used tensor-based morphometry (TBM), a whole-brain voxelwise morphometric method closely related to VBM, with scans registered to ICBM stereotaxic space (i.e., MNI-like) and reported voxel-wise between-group contrasts and voxel-wise regressions (figures and ROI analyses). Sample sizes exceed the minimum. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are reported and clearly identified for the target bvFTD group. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

The study reports voxelwise FDG-PET analyses (SPM) with group-level whole-brain results (group SPM analysis and a one-sample t-test on impaired patients) overlaid on an MNI template, fulfilling imaging modality and spatial reporting requirements. The sample comprises 17 clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (meets minimum N), and analyses include comparisons against a normative database producing voxelwise contrasts in standard space. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not DTI/FC-only, empirical data, and no evidence of disallowed comorbid sample). Therefore the paper satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

Although the study includes a bvFTD sample (n=15) and reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses, the neuroimaging methods are cortical thickness / ANTs-based structural MRI analyses rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET required by the inclusion criteria. Exclusion criterion E6 disallows studies that only report cortical thickness methods. In addition, the reported whole-brain voxelwise imaging results and coordinate peaks pertain to svPPA patients, not to the bvFTD group (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results are clearly reported for bvFTD), so the study does not provide the target-sample whole-brain contrasts required (I7). Therefore it fails to meet required imaging-modality and whole-brain results criteria for inclusion.

The study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and FDG‑PET whole-brain voxelwise analyses comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients to healthy controls (and bipolar patients). Sample sizes (bvFTD n=23 initial, n=21 in MRI analysis; PET n=23) exceed the minimum. Results are reported in stereotactic space (MNI, converted to Talairach) with cluster coordinates and tables/figures referenced. The full text includes introduction, methods (imaging acquisition and voxelwise SPM analyses), results (group contrasts and coordinates), and discussion, so core content is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI‑only results, prohibited modalities, or disallowed comorbid samples) apply. Therefore the paper meets all required inclusion criteria for the review and should be included.

Although the paper includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=11) and adequate sample size for that group, it does NOT use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. The imaging method is structural MRI with visual atrophy rating scales (qualitative scores). The study does not report any voxelwise, whole-brain between-group contrasts in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables/voxelwise statistical maps. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 and must be excluded. Full text appears complete and provides methods/results/discussion, but lacks the required imaging modality and whole-brain voxelwise results.

Although this study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=14) and applies VBM methods alongside DTI, it does not report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in a stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) that would meet the review’s I6/I7 requirements. The VBM procedure described was applied with an anterior cingulate mask to extract mean gray matter density for the ACC (an ROI-based approach) rather than reporting whole-brain voxelwise coordinates or tables. The paper’s primary analyses focus on tractography (DTI) and on ACC-specific measures; thus it effectively only provides ROI/masked results and lacks the required whole-brain voxelwise contrasts. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (uses VBM), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD), and I5 (sample sizes ≥6), but fails to meet I6 and I7 and is excluded based on E3 (reports only ROI/masked analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

The full text includes VBM analysis (grey matter voxel-based morphometry) in addition to DTI, reports whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons projected to MNI space, and explicitly presents group-level whole-brain results (FWE-corrected) for bvFTD versus controls and AD. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=27) and healthy and AD comparison groups (≥6 subjects per group). Results are reported as voxelwise maps and described in text/figures/tables. The manuscript contains complete core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and does not trigger any exclusion criteria.

This empirical study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=26) and healthy controls, uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with images normalized to MNI space, and reports group-level whole-brain VBM comparisons and voxelwise regression analyses linking GM atrophy to behavioral measures. Sample sizes exceed the minimum threshold. Whole-brain voxelwise results are described (clusters in OFC, amygdala, APC, temporal lobes) and analyses were conducted in MNI space; supplementary materials with further results are referenced. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses, reviews, non-empirical, comorbid psychiatric/neuro diagnoses, or disallowed modalities) are violated.

This is a single-case clinical report (n=1) of probable bvFTD that includes 18F-FDG PET imaging. While it meets I3 (FDG-PET used) and I4 (patient clinically diagnosed with bvFTD), it fails key inclusion criteria required for the meta-analysis: I5 (minimum sample size of ≥6 participants in patient or control group is not met), I6 (no between-group contrast reported in MNI/Talairach space), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results; only single-subject/visual PET description). None of the formal exclusion criteria (E2–E6) specifically apply, but per the review rules any unmet inclusion criterion mandates exclusion. Full text appears complete for a case report (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=14) and adequate sample size, it does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET as the primary imaging modality. The neuroimaging analyses are ROI-based using FreeSurfer cortical volumes and DTI-derived FA/MD and WM volumes (atlas ROIs). The paper does not report whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts in stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) space or provide voxelwise coordinate tables/figures; analyses are ROI-based. Therefore the study fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 and meets exclusion criteria E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and E6 (reports DTI and cortical-volume/thickness methods rather than VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET). Full text appears complete.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusions: it uses voxel-based morphometry/anatomical MRI and resting-state fMRI (and DTI) (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=23) (I4) with sufficient sample size (I5).
