The imaging processing and statistics were performed in standard stereotactic space (registration to MNI152 template and TBSS/FMRIB58_FA template) and whole-brain, voxelwise pipelines (VBM, TBSS, ICA-based rs-fMRI) are described; group-level, whole-brain results and region-level findings are reported and tied to MNI-based analyses (I6, I7). The paper provides full text with methods, results, and discussion; while exact coordinate tables are not visible in the provided excerpt, the methods explicitly reference MNI-space processing and whole-brain voxelwise procedures and supplemental material is indicated for additional results (I8). Therefore the study should be included for the bvFTD imaging review.

This empirical study includes clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD patients and uses FDG-PET (satisfying I3, I4, I5). However, it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) nor provide coordinate tables or voxelwise statistical maps. The analysis centers on individual Z-maps and visual reader performance metrics (sensitivity, specificity, kappa) rather than voxelwise group comparisons. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7 requiring between-group voxelwise results. The full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it uses voxel-based morphometry and task-free (resting-state) fMRI (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with sample sizes of 14 patients per bvFTD subgroup and 14 controls (I5); reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts using standard spatial normalization (MNI template) and voxelwise statistical maps/thresholding (I6, I7). Whole-brain results are presented in figures and referred to supplementary materials (acceptable per I8). No exclusion criteria apply: this is original empirical work (not a review), includes whole-brain voxelwise analyses (not ROI-only), and does not rely solely on modalities excluded by E6. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Given the detailed voxelwise group results and imaging modalities, the study should be INCLUDED.

The full text reports voxelwise whole-brain gray matter analyses (GMP images, transformed to MNI space) using ANTs and FSL Randomise, i.e., VBM-style methods; includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=54) and healthy controls; sample sizes exceed 6; reports group-level whole-brain contrasts (patient groups vs controls) and whole-brain regression analyses with results in stereotactic (MNI) space and supplementary materials. The paper contains complete methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI analyses, review article, restricted modalities) apply.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with DARTEL/SPM preprocessing and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons (bvFTD vs controls, BD vs controls, bvFTD vs BD) normalized to MNI space. The sample includes 16 clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (meets diagnostic criteria) and group sizes exceed the minimum (16 bvFTD, 13 BD, 22 controls). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are reported (FWE-corrected, p<0.05) and regions/atrophy patterns are described. No exclusion criteria are violated (not a review; not ROI-only; uses VBM; patient sample appropriate). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This empirical study includes 35 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and uses voxel-based morphometry and resting-state fMRI analyses. Whole-brain VBM results are reported (FWE-corrected clusters with coordinates provided in SI Appendix), and seed-based functional connectivity analyses are also presented. Sample sizes exceed the minimum threshold. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results from the target patient group. No exclusion criteria are violated. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=11), uses VBM, and reports voxelwise peak coordinates in MNI space, the VBM analysis was performed within a predefined fronto‑striatal ROI mask rather than as an unrestricted whole‑brain voxelwise analysis. The review's exclusion criterion E3 disqualifies studies that report only ROI‑restricted analyses with no whole‑brain results. Therefore the study does not meet the requirement for at least one group-level whole‑brain (voxelwise) result and must be excluded.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (N=18). The paper uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality, includes at least 6 participants per group, and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results with cluster peaks and MNI coordinates (SPM8 results, cluster- and voxel-thresholds described). Whole-brain contrasts and correlations (e.g., AD vs bvFTD, and merged-group voxelwise regressions) are clearly reported in the text, figures and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria are violated (not a review, not ROI-only, no disqualifying comorbid sample, not a methods-only paper). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on T1-weighted MRI (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient sample (N=15) and healthy controls (I4, I5), reports whole-brain voxelwise group analyses (two-sample t-test and multiple regressions) with results given in MNI coordinates (e.g., peak MNI-coordinates reported) (I6, I7), and whole-brain results are clearly described and shown in figures/tables (I8). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only analyses, prohibited modalities, or disallowed comorbid samples) apply. Therefore the study should be included.

This is an empirical study that uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts overlaid on the MNI standard brain (I6, I7, I8). The sample includes clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD patients (I4) with n=15 in the in vivo cohort (I5), and adequate control and Alzheimer’s groups. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply: it is not a review (E2), it reports whole-brain VBM results rather than ROI-only (not E3), participants do not have excluded comorbidities reported (not E4), it is empirical original data (not E5), and although DTI is included the study also uses VBM rather than only DTI/FC/cortical thickness (not E6). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and should be included.

The study used manual segmentation and shape/volume analysis of striatal structures from structural MRI (T1-weighted) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET, therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I3. Analyses are region-of-interest (caudate and putamen) based and do not report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results or stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach), so it fails I6/I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (n=28) and sufficient sample size, and the full text appears complete; however, the imaging modality and ROI-only reporting warrant exclusion from this review.

This paper reports task-based fMRI (I3) in a sample of clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD patients (Neary and revised criteria) (I4) with n=20 patients and n=18 controls (I5). The authors conducted voxel-wise, whole-brain group contrasts (with voxel-wise gray-matter covariate correction) and report peak coordinates in standard space (MNI/Talairach) in tables and figures (I6, I7). Whole-brain results are clearly described in the text and tables (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not an excluded modality, and comorbidities were excluded). Full article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations) are present, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Although this empirical study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=22) (I4) with adequate sample sizes (I5), and reports voxelwise results with MNI coordinates (I6/I8), the VBM analyses were performed within an a priori region-of-interest mask limited to prefrontal cortex and medial temporal lobe. Because the paper reports only ROI-masked voxelwise results rather than whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise analyses, it falls under the review exclusion for studies that present only ROI (non-whole-brain) analyses. Therefore it does not meet the whole-brain evidence requirement and must be excluded.

The study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=20) and used FDG-PET as an imaging modality; it therefore meets I3, I4, and I5. However, the full text presents FDG/PiB-PET only as diagnostic biomarkers and does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise imaging analyses or between-group contrasts with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. Inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (coordinate-based between-group contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results) are not satisfied. The paper is an empirical study with complete core sections, but lacks the required voxelwise imaging results needed for inclusion in the meta-analysis, so it must be excluded.

The study uses [18F]-FDG-PET (FDG-PET) with voxel-wise SPM8 analyses normalized to MNI space and reports whole-brain voxelwise results (clusters and coordinates) correlating metabolism with theory-of-mind deficits. The sample includes clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD patients (n=11) alongside controls and Alzheimer’s patients (all groups ≥6), and PET analyses are reported at the group level for the target sample. Therefore it satisfies the imaging modality, bvFTD sample, minimum sample size, voxelwise coordinate reporting, and whole-brain group-level result requirements. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, excluded modalities, comorbid psychiatric/neurological confounds) apply.

Although the study used VBM (preprocessing and normalization to MNI space) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with adequate sample size, it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts or coordinate tables in MNI/Talairach space. The authors extracted GM volumes using a priori masks (ROI-based extraction) for classification rather than presenting voxelwise whole-brain results. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise reporting and must be excluded.

This empirical study used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports voxelwise group-level contrasts and correlations with episodic memory using MNI stereotaxic space. It includes a clearly clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=19) and matched controls (n=19) and AD patients (n=18), meeting sample size requirements. Whole-brain VBM results are reported (figures and tables with MNI coordinates) and overlap/exclusive masking analyses are described. The full-text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses, reviews, comorbid psychiatric or substance-abuse samples) are violated. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review objective.

The study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=22), uses VBM, reports MNI coordinates, and meets sample size requirements (I3, I4, I5, I6). However, all neuroimaging analyses were conducted within an a priori cortical midline structures (CMS) region-of-interest mask rather than as whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The methods and results indicate an ROI-based VBM approach and do not present whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results outside the CMS mask. Therefore the study meets the exclusion criterion for studies that report only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results (E3). Full text appears complete.

This study does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. It does not include clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD)—the sample comprises primary progressive aphasia (PPA) variants (semantic dementia, progressive nonfluent aphasia, and one logopenic case) and Alzheimer’s disease and healthy controls. Also, the imaging modality is dual-phase 18F-florbetapir PET (amyloid/perfusion-like), not one of the required modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). Although the study has adequate sample sizes (PPA n=6, AD n=8, HC n=8) and reports whole-brain, voxel-wise SPM results in MNI space, failure to satisfy I3 and I4 means it cannot be included in this bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

The study does not meet the imaging-modality inclusion criterion (I3). It uses structural longitudinal MRI analyses (tensor-based morphometry, boundary-shift integral) rather than VBM, fMRI (resting/task), or FDG-PET as required. The paper does include clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4), has adequate sample sizes (I5), and reports whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons (I6/I7) using SPM5; full text appears complete. Because failure to meet the modality requirement is sufficient for exclusion, the study should be excluded.

The study uses FDG-PET imaging (voxel-wise SPM analyses) in a sample of 37 clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients, which exceeds the minimum sample size. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were performed (comparison of patient scans vs a control database to identify hypometabolism and regression analyses relating FDG-PET to occupation PCA scores), with reported clusters and FWE thresholding. These satisfy imaging modality (I3), bvFTD sample (I4), sample size (I5), reporting of voxelwise whole-brain group results from the target sample (I7), and between-group contrast against controls for hypometabolism (I6). Results are described in the text/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria were met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical VBM study reporting whole-brain voxelwise results in a defined stereotactic space. The sample includes clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD patients (n=21) and meets the minimum sample size threshold. The study uses voxel-based morphometry (SPM5/DARTEL) as the imaging modality and reports group-level, whole-brain results (figures and tables with corrected cluster results and coordinates). Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review, ROI-only, non-empirical, prohibited modalities, or comorbid psychiatric diagnoses) are met. Therefore the paper satisfies all relevant inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study employed resting-state fMRI (ICA, fALFF, REHO, seed-based and PLS) satisfying imaging modality requirements. The sample included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=8) alongside controls, meeting the bvFTD and sample-size criteria (>6). Analyses used whole-brain voxelwise SPM random-effects ANOVA with multiple-comparison correction and report peak voxel coordinates (e.g., BA46 peak x=36,y=42,z=30), satisfying the between-group contrast in a defined stereotactic space and whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria are met.

Study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and uses FDG-PET, and sample sizes meet minimum; however, the full text does not report any between-group voxelwise results with coordinates in a defined stereotactic space (MNI or Talairach) for the bvFTD group. Methods state SPM8 normalization to MNI space and voxelwise testing, but no tables or coordinate lists or clear voxelwise, whole-brain, group-level contrast results in MNI/Talairach for bvFTD are provided in the supplied full text. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: it does not use VBM, fMRI (resting/task), or FDG-PET. Instead it uses deformation-based morphometry (DBM) and arterial spin labeling (ASL) perfusion MRI with joint-ICA. The paper does include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12) and provides whole-brain voxelwise group analyses (satisfying I4, I5, I7), but the imaging modality requirement (I3) is not met. The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). I6 (reporting of coordinates in MNI/Talairach) is not clearly satisfied in the provided content (region lists are given but coordinate tables are not shown), so it is not claimed as met. Therefore the study must be excluded.

The full text reports a voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analysis using SPM12 comparing bvFTD patients with mild AD and reports whole-brain voxelwise results (displayed at family-wise error corrected p<0.05). The participant sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=220 randomized; MITT n=214), exceeding the minimum sample size. The paper provides group-level, whole-brain between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs AD) presented in figures and described in text. While coordinate tables are not explicitly quoted in the excerpt, the VBM results are reported as voxelwise, whole-brain analyses and are acceptable per inclusion allowance for figures/supplementary reporting. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses, reviews, non-empirical work, or disallowed modalities) apply. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) patients (n=27) with healthy controls. Voxel-based morphometry was applied and whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported, including MNI coordinates for peak effects and tables/figures; they also performed ROI/SVC analyses but whole-brain results are present. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). The full text includes introduction, methods (behavioral and imaging), results with MNI coordinates, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, non-VBM modality, or major comorbidities) are met.

This is an original empirical study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (SPM8/DARTEL) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results (voxelwise threshold p<0.001, pFWE<0.05) in MNI space. The sample includes 31 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, plus other patient groups and 75 controls, meeting the minimum sample size requirement. The paper provides voxelwise between-group/covariate analyses and reports peak regions (tables/figures) and performs co-atrophy checks, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not ROI-only; not seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness only; no disqualifying comorbid sample issues noted). Therefore, all relevant inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are met.

This is an original, empirical study that uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (FSL-VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts mapped to MNI standard space. The sample includes clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) patients (n=14) as well as Alzheimer’s disease patients and controls, meeting the minimum sample-size requirement. The paper presents whole-brain VBM results (group contrasts and covariate analyses) and reports clusters/figures overlaid on the MNI template; results are reported in tables/figures and described in the text. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so the article is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (reviews, ROI-only, non-empirical, or exclusive DTI/FC/cortical-thickness-only methods) apply.

This paper is a study protocol (NIMROD) describing planned multimodal imaging in multiple dementia cohorts including FTD (criteria referenced to Rascovsky, which targets behavioral-variant FTD). The protocol includes resting-state fMRI and plans for group sizes >=16, so it meets I3 (fMRI), I4 (FTD/bvFTD cohort inclusion is implied), and I5 (sample size). However, it reports no empirical results: there are no between-group contrasts, no reported voxelwise coordinates in MNI/Talairach space, and no whole-brain group-level results (planned analyses only). Therefore it fails I6 and I7. As a protocol/non-empirical paper without original data, it falls under exclusion criterion E5. Full text appears complete (protocol with methods but no results).

This study is excluded because it does not meet key imaging-modality and reporting criteria for the review. The imaging analysis uses structural MRI with Freesurfer-derived cortical thickness/volumetric measures (surface-based morphometry), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (violating I3). The paper does not report between-group voxelwise coordinates in a standard stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach), so criterion I6 is not satisfied. The patient sample includes only five VSM-20 family members with MRI (failing the >=6-patient requirement for the target analyzed group), and the study’s patient cohort also includes comorbid neurological syndromes (ALS, parkinsonism, corticobasal features), violating the requirement for a pure bvFTD sample (E4). Finally, the imaging results are based on cortical thickness/volumetric methods rather than the required modalities, so E6 applies. Full text appears complete. Exclusion based on E4 and E6; inclusion criteria I4 and I5 (presence of clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants and at least 6 bvFTD participants in the sporadic bvFTD comparison group) are present, but the modality and reporting requirements are not met.

Although the study includes FDG-PET imaging (I3) and a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient sample (I4) with N=8 (I5), it does not report any between-group contrasts in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) nor provide group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables. The imaging findings are described qualitatively (hypometabolism on PET/SPECT) in a case series format without reported voxelwise statistical maps or coordinates, so criteria I6 and I7 are not met. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Although this paper includes bvFTD patients and uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with whole-brain voxelwise SPM results in MNI space, the VBM analyses are reported as correlations across the entire pooled sample (brain–behavior regressions) rather than as a clear group-level, whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrast specific to the bvFTD group. The manuscript does not present voxelwise, group-level (bvFTD vs controls) coordinate results that are clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD sample, so it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7. Other inclusion criteria are met (VBM modality, bvFTD sample, adequate sample size, and results presented in figures/tables), but the lack of a bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise contrast prevents inclusion in the meta-analysis focused on group-level imaging results.

This is an original empirical study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=26) and healthy controls. Imaging modalities include voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and resting-state fMRI connectivity; VBM methods used SPM/DARTEL with normalization to MNI space and report whole-brain voxelwise results and peak coordinates (supplementary tables/figures). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts associating SOIS with grey matter volume in bvFTD and provides coordinates and thresholding. Sample sizes exceed the minimum. The full text contains Introduction, Methods (participants, MRI acquisition, VBM, fMRI preprocessing), Results (voxelwise VBM, VLSM, functional connectivity), and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (reviews, ROI-only, non-empirical, comorbidities, or prohibited modalities) are met. Therefore the study satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

This empirical study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=17 in main analyses) and healthy controls, uses resting-state fMRI and voxel-wise structural analyses, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (with coordinates/SI Appendix), and provides voxel-wise correlation and between-group contrasts. Sample size exceeds the minimum (>=6). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and does not appear to include excluded designs (not a review, not ROI-only, not only seed-based FC/DTI/thickness). Therefore it meets all listed inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The study reports empirical whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (structural MRI) with bvFTD patients (n=24) and controls, and provides group-level voxelwise results with MNI coordinates. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). Methods include whole-brain GLM with permutation testing and TFCE; neuroanatomical results and coordinates are reported in tables/figures. Exclusion criteria (e.g., comorbid psychiatric disorders, ROI-only analyses) are not violated. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all imaging, sample, and reporting inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The full text reports a study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=19) and healthy controls (N=20). Imaging modalities include voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and task-based fMRI. Whole-brain, voxelwise VBM group comparisons (normalized to MNI space) are reported (FWE-corrected results) and whole-brain fMRI analyses and group contrasts are described. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). Results are reported in a defined stochastic space (MNI) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise findings are clearly identified. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, disallowed modalities) apply.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=7 per patient subgroup) and provides full methods/results, it uses structural MRI with Freesurfer-derived ROI volumetry (orbitofrontal and middle frontal gyrus volumes) rather than VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET. The paper reports region-of-interest volumetric comparisons (cm^3) and does not present whole-brain voxelwise results or between-group coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12 at baseline) and uses resting-state fMRI and DTI, the analyses are tract-specific (DTI tractography) and ROI-based functional connectivity. The paper does not report any whole-brain voxelwise group-level results or stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) for between-group contrasts; results are reported as tract-wise metrics and ROI connectivity matrices/figures. Therefore it fails the requirement for voxelwise/whole-brain coordinate results (I6/I7) and meets exclusion criteria for reporting only ROI/tract-based analyses and DTI/seed-based FC methods (E3, E6). Full text appears complete.

This empirical study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=19) and uses Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) with whole-brain, voxelwise analyses reported (coordinates, thresholding) in MNI space. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD n=19; controls n=20). The paper reports group-level whole-brain results and neuroimaging-behavior correlations with coordinates and statistical thresholds, satisfying the meta-analysis imaging and reporting requirements. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, neuroimaging details) is present.

Although the study used FDG-PET and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=27), it does not report any voxelwise, whole-brain between-group contrasts or stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach). Imaging assessments were visual ratings and diagnostic classifications rather than voxel-based or statistical parametric maps. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (at least one between-group contrast in defined stereotactic space and a group-level whole-brain voxelwise result) are not met. No other exclusion criteria appear triggered.

This paper is a study protocol / design paper for the ongoing LOF study and does not report empirical whole-brain neuroimaging results required by the meta-analysis. Although FDG-PET and MRI are planned as modalities, no between-group contrasts, voxelwise (MNI/Talairach) coordinates, VBM, or fMRI results are reported. The sample is defined by late-onset frontal behavioral symptoms rather than a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group, and no group-level whole-brain results are provided. Therefore it does not meet the inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I6, I7) and qualifies as a non-empirical methods/design paper without original imaging results (E5).

The full text reports an empirical multicenter study including 52 clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients and 60 controls, using resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM). Analyses include whole-brain, voxelwise VBM (normalized to MNI space) and whole-brain functional connectivity/graph-theory results with group-level between-group contrasts reported (figures and supporting tables). Sample sizes exceed the minimum. The paper provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results clearly attributed to the bvFTD sample and supplies coordinates/normalized-space analyses (MNI). Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are violated. Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria for the review.

This empirical study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=14) and uses voxel-based morphometry and resting-state/task-based fMRI. It reports voxelwise, whole-brain group comparisons and voxel coordinates (e.g., left ATL [-45,13,-37], left IFG [-52,2,14]) in MNI space and presents group-level VBM and connectivity results for the bvFTD sample. Sample size meets the ≥6 requirement. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review only, ROI-only, exclusive methods like DTI-only, or comorbid psychiatric samples) are met. Therefore the paper satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes a clinical FTLD sample with a substantial subgroup diagnosed as behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) (21/29), satisfying the requirement that bvFTD patients are included (I4). Sample sizes meet the threshold (FTLD n=29; controls n=30) (I5). The imaging analysis used SPM and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates referenced in standard space (MNI/Talairach) in tables and figures (I6, I7, I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only results, seed-based FC/DTI-only methods, or comorbid psychiatric/substance-abuse confounds) are violated. Therefore the paper meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Although this study used VBM (I3), included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and had >=6 patients (I5), it does not report any between-group (patient vs control) voxelwise contrasts in a standard space. The voxelwise analyses were restricted to a frontal mask (region-restricted VBM) and report within-group correlations between gray matter volume and behavioral scores with MNI coordinates; however, no whole-brain, group-level between-group results are presented. Therefore it fails the required inclusion criteria I6 and I7, and the analysis effectively constitutes a region-of-interest/masked voxelwise analysis, meeting exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete.

Although the full text is complete and the study includes clinically-diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12), uses resting-state fMRI and reports whole-brain voxelwise TBSS and functional connectivity results, it reports only diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and seed-based resting-state functional connectivity analyses. The review’s exclusion criterion E6 disqualifies studies that only report seed-based FC, DTI, or cortical thickness methods. Therefore, despite satisfying multiple inclusion requirements (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8), the study must be excluded because it only uses modalities/methods listed in E6.

The study is a prospective clinical study of late-onset frontal lobe syndrome including clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=55) and reports use of FDG-PET as part of diagnostic workup. However, it does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) imaging analyses or provide coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. No VBM or fMRI voxelwise results or tables of stereotactic coordinates are presented. Therefore it fails the review’s required imaging outcome criteria (no whole-brain voxelwise results), and must be excluded.

The study directly investigates FTD including clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (11 patients) using FDG-PET (alongside ASL-MRI). Sample sizes meet the minimum (≥6 per group). Images were normalized to MNI space and the paper reports voxelwise t-maps and group-level comparisons (voxelwise and ROI), providing whole-brain, between-group results clearly identified for the patient group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, inappropriate modalities, or comorbid samples) are violated.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=22) and reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain VBM results in standard space (MNI). Imaging modality: VBM (satisfies I3). Sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and sufficient sample size (I4, I5). The paper reports between-group contrasts and covariate analyses with results localized in MNI coordinates and shown in figures/tables (I6, I8). Voxelwise GLM and permutation testing with FWE/FDR correction across frontal/temporal masks constitute whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results from the target sample (I7). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, not only other modalities).

Although the study uses FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), has a control group of n=10 satisfying the minimum group size (I5), and reports voxelwise SPM analyses in MNI space (I6), it does NOT provide any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) between-group results for the bvFTD sample (only single-subject SPM contrasts and ROI summaries). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 (no group-level whole-brain result from the target sample). Additionally, the bvFTD subgroup size is only n=4, limiting group-level inference for the target population. Based on these deficiencies the study is excluded from the meta-analysis focused on group-level whole-brain bvFTD contrasts.

This is a clinical symptom comparison study that used SPECT/FDG-PET only to support diagnoses; it did not perform VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or voxelwise FDG-PET group analyses and did not report any whole-brain, stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) between-group coordinates. Although the sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases (n=4 within FTD group) and patient group sizes exceed 6, the study fails to meet imaging-analysis inclusion criteria (I3, I6, I7). Therefore it cannot contribute the required whole-brain neuroimaging coordinate data for the meta-analysis.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (and reports voxelwise group comparisons after normalization to MNI space), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (final bvFTD n=24), has adequate sample size (>6 participants), and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (FWE-corrected VBM and TBSS results) that are clearly described. Whole-brain results are presented in the text and figures/ROIs were extracted from thresholded T-maps, consistent with acceptable reporting (including supplementary exploration). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review only, ROI-only, only DTI/FC methods, or samples with disallowed comorbidities) are triggered by the content. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=9) and sufficient sample size, it does not use the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) specified by the review inclusion criteria. The primary imaging methods are diffusion tensor imaging (DTI/TBSS and tractography), structural MRI volumetry (ROI-based multiatlas measures), and arterial spin labeling (ASL) perfusion. The review’s I3 criterion requires VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; therefore the study does not meet I3 and should be excluded. Full text is complete and contains methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical, whole-brain VBM study of bvFTD including 24 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and 179 controls. It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), has ≥6 participants in the patient group (I5), reports voxelwise between-group and interaction results with MNI coordinates (I6), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise findings clearly in the text and figures/tables (I7,I8). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply based on provided information. Replication and longitudinal recommendations noted but do not affect eligibility.

The study employed voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and reports whole‑brain voxelwise group analyses with MNI coordinates (I6, I7). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=11) (I4) and meets the minimum sample-size requirement (I5); results are reported in figures/tables and text (I8). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria are violated (e.g., it is an original empirical study, not ROI-only, and includes VBM rather than only DTI/FC). Therefore the paper qualifies for inclusion.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (I3 satisfied), includes clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD patients (I4 satisfied) and has adequate sample sizes (I5 satisfied). However, the voxel-based morphometry analyses reported are performed and presented for pathologically defined subgroups (e.g., Pick’s, MAPT, TDP-A, TDP-C, FUS) relative to healthy controls, not for the clinical bvFTD group as a whole. The paper does not report a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrast specifically identified as coming from the target clinical bvFTD sample (I7 not met). Although whole-brain VBM contrasts are reported for pathological groups (likely in standard space; I6 likely met), they do not provide whole-brain voxelwise results for the bvFTD clinical group required by the review objective. Therefore the study fails to meet the requirement that at least one whole-brain, voxelwise result is reported for the target (bvFTD) sample and must be excluded.

This is an empirical resting-state fMRI study (fALFF and REHO) that prospectively enrolled patients with frontotemporal dementia including clinically-diagnosed bvFTD (5 bvFTD, 10 SD) and age-matched healthy controls. Total patient N=15 and control N=16 meet the sample-size requirement. The authors performed whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts to identify ROIs (reported as eTable 1 and described in the text/figures) and used those results in subsequent analyses, indicating group-level, whole-brain voxelwise findings (supplementary tables/figures are referenced). The paper includes introduction, methods, results and discussion (full text present). Therefore the study meets the imaging modality, patient sample, sample size, between-group coordinate/voxelwise result, whole-brain evidence, and allowance for reporting in supplementary materials. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD subgroup (bvFTD; n=17) within the FTD sample, satisfying the bvFTD sample requirement. Imaging modality is voxel-based morphometry (VBM). Sample sizes meet the minimum (FTD n=52, AD n=20, controls n=18). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level VBM results identified for the FTD group and provides results in MNI space (e.g., left superior frontal gyrus coordinates x=-10,y=28,z=60), fulfilling the coordinate reporting requirement. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses, reviews, non-empirical) are triggered. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This study does not meet the required imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting criteria for inclusion. The authors do not clearly specify that the FTD cases are behavioral-variant, and the number of FTD cases (4) is below the minimum sample threshold (>=6) for the patient subgroup of interest. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample of interest) and the practical requirement of sufficient bvFTD sample size. Full text appears complete.

Imaging and analysis do not meet inclusion criteria: the study uses manual volumetric ROI measurements from structural MRI rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 unmet). Analyses are ROI-based and do not report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results or stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach), so no between-group voxelwise contrasts are available (I6/I7 unmet; E3 applies). Sample size is adequate (49 FTD patients; I5 met). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper cannot be included in a coordinate-based, whole-brain meta-analysis of bvFTD imaging studies.

This empirical study used Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) (I3) and explicitly included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=11) (I4). Sample sizes meet the threshold (bvFTD n=11; controls and other groups also ≥6) (I5). VBM preprocessing was performed in Talairach space and group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported with coordinates and corrected cluster results (I6, I7). Results are presented in figures and tables and described in the text (I8). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment of imaging methods and group contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and not using only excluded modalities). Therefore the paper satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the review on bvFTD imaging.

This empirical study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses comparing bvFTD patients and controls and between-genotype groups, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (15 C9+ and 48 noncarriers) and healthy controls (n≈63), and presents whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results (interaction and main effects reported with pFWE thresholds and referenced coordinate tables/figures). Core article content (methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets imaging modality (VBM), bvFTD sample, adequate sample size, and whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements.

This full text reports an empirical, whole-brain, voxelwise multimodal imaging study combining VBM (SPM5) and FDG-PET in a sample of 15 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (Rascovsky criteria) and 15 matched healthy controls. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). The paper presents group-level voxelwise between-group contrasts and voxelwise correlation/contrast analyses (SPM, z-score maps) reported as statistical maps and tables/figures (whole-brain MNI-normalized analyses). The study is not a review, not ROI-only, and does not include excluded comorbid samples. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality, included a clinically diagnosed FTD group corresponding to behavioral-variant FTD (classified using Neary criteria), had adequate group sizes (FTD N=8; controls N=20), and reported whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts with anatomical localization referenced to standard space (Talairach/MNI) and tables/figures describing the results. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion sufficient to confirm whole-brain voxelwise findings for the target sample. No exclusion criteria are evident (not a review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, not an excluded modality, and no indication of disqualifying comorbid psychiatric or other dementia samples). Therefore the study should be included.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=35) and uses [18F]FDG-PET in its diagnostic workup (satisfying I3, I4, I5), it does not report any voxel-wise, whole-brain group-level analyses or between-group contrasts in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). Imaging findings are reported qualitatively (rated as normal/abnormal) and used for clinical diagnosis rather than as coordinate-based statistical results. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. This study lacks whole-brain voxelwise results and thus falls under exclusion criterion E3 (no whole-brain results / only non-voxelwise imaging reporting). Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study is excluded because it does not meet the required imaging-modality inclusion criterion (I3). The study used F-Flortaucipir tau-PET and autoradiography, not one of the eligible modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). Other inclusion criteria are met: it includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (C9orf72 mutation carriers), has at least 6 patients, reports voxel-wise between-group contrasts in MNI space, and provides whole-brain voxelwise results for the bvFTD group. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply based on the provided full text. Full text appears complete.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and reports voxel-wise, whole-brain PET comparisons versus controls, it does NOT use one of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). The study uses F-THK5351 tau PET (a tau/MAO-B tracer), which falls outside the eligible modalities per I3. All other relevant inclusion criteria are met (clinical bvFTD sample, adequate control group size, and voxel-wise between-group results), and the full text appears complete. Because failure to meet I3 is sufficient for exclusion, the study is excluded.

This study uses structural T1-weighted MRI volumetric analysis (automated basal forebrain segmentation using GIF) rather than Voxel-Based Morphometry, fMRI, or FDG-PET, so it fails the required imaging-modality inclusion criterion (I3). Although it includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4) with sufficient sample size (148 bvFTD; I5), the paper reports region-based volumetric results rather than whole-brain, voxelwise results in a defined stereotactic space (no MNI/Talairach coordinate tables or voxelwise contrasts), thus failing I6 and I7. Therefore it meets the exclusion criterion for reporting only ROI/region volumetry with no whole-brain voxelwise results (E3).

This VBM study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (bvFTD subgroup n=45) and reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM results versus controls. It therefore satisfies I3 (VBM), I4 (bvFTD sample), I5 (sample size ≥6), and I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (MNI or Talairach) or explicitly state results in a defined stereotactic space, so I6 cannot be confirmed from the supplied content. Because all inclusion criteria must be verifiable and I6 is unmet, the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=15) (I4,I5), reports group-level between-group contrasts normalized to MNI space using SPM/DARTEL (I6), and presents whole-brain voxelwise results (e.g., contrasts thresholded at P<0.05 FWE whole-brain) clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD vs control groups (I7). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, no disallowed modalities or comorbid samples).

This study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports voxelwise SPM results in standard stereotactic space (MNI) (coordinates/supplementary table referenced). The sample includes 32 FTLD patients, specifically 19 patients meeting clinical criteria for behavioural variant FTD (bvFTD), and 22 healthy controls (all groups >6 participants). Group-level, voxelwise analyses (behavioural regressions within the FTLD cohort and subgroup contrasts) are reported and small-volume corrected significant associations are presented, with results displayed in standard space. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental tables are noted but their absence does not render the core text incomplete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only analyses, non-empirical work, or disallowed imaging modalities) apply. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the review of bvFTD imaging studies.

The study is a methods paper applying a unified VBM/TBM approach to groups including frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patients (N=30), Alzheimer’s disease, and controls, with whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses. However, the FTD sample is not specified as clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD). The review’s I4 criterion requires inclusion of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; because the paper reports only FTD without specifying bvFTD subtype, it does not meet I4 and must be excluded. Other inclusion criteria are met (VBM/TBM imaging modality, adequate sample size, whole-brain voxelwise results reported), and the full text appears complete.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses resting-state fMRI and VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within the sample (7 bvFTD cases; I4), has sufficient sample size (14 FTD-GRN+ patients and healthy groups; I5), reports between-group voxelwise contrasts with MNI coordinates and cluster statistics (I6), and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results clearly attributed to the target groups (I7). Results are reported as figures/coordinates (I8). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses, reviews, seed-only FC, DTI-only, comorbid psychiatric samples) are violated based on provided content.

This paper reports an empirical FDG-PET study of patients diagnosed with the frontal variant of frontotemporal dementia (fv-FTD), an established synonym/older term for behavioral-variant FTD. The study used voxel-wise SPM2 analyses with Talairach-based localization and reports whole-brain voxelwise correlations (tables/figures of clusters and coordinates). Sample sizes meet the minimum (fv-FTD n=18; controls n=18). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (i.e., core article content) and no exclusion criteria are violated (not a review; not ROI-only; not seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness only; comorbidities excluded). Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons in MNI space (I6,I7,I8). The sample includes 18 clinically defined ALS-FTD patients (diagnosed by Neary criteria) and 15 controls, meeting the minimum group size (I5). ALS-FTD patients were defined using Neary criteria for frontotemporal dementia, which corresponds to clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD in many studies; thus they satisfy the review’s requirement for bvFTD patients (I4). The full text includes background, methods, results and discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be included.

The study reports longitudinal 18F-FDG-PET (FDG-PET) voxelwise analyses (SPM) on clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTD (behavioral variant equivalent) with 22 patients and 15 controls. It provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts and reports maxima in Talairach space. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. It meets all required inclusion criteria (imaging modality, clinical diagnosis, sample size, coordinate reporting, whole-brain voxelwise results). No exclusion criteria are violated.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on MRI and reports group-level whole-brain VBM contrasts with MNI coordinates, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (Neary criteria) with adequate sample sizes (FTD N=26; MRI subset FTD N=21, controls N=12), and provides whole-brain voxelwise results and coordinate tables/figures. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment. No exclusion criteria are met. Thus it satisfies all imaging, sample size, diagnostic, and reporting criteria for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This study does not address the review objective of bvFTD. Participants were patients with semantic dementia / svPPA with post-mortem-confirmed TDP-43 type C pathology, not clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (fails I4). The imaging modality is T1-weighted structural MRI with region-of-interest volumetric analyses (w-scores) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3). The analyses are ROI-based regional volume results, not whole-brain voxelwise results in standard space (violates I6/I7) — thus it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be excluded.

This is an empirical study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) that includes a clinically diagnosed behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) cohort (n=10). Sample sizes meet the minimum (≥6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise VBM contrasts and discusses results in MNI/DARTEL template space; VBM outputs and comparisons to controls are presented. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This empirical study includes clinically-diagnosed bvFTD participants from a MAPT mutation family (8 symptomatic bvFTD patients, 3 asymptomatic carriers, and 8 non-carrier controls). It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and [18F]FDG PET imaging, performs whole-brain voxel-wise group comparisons using SPM8 normalized to MNI space, and reports voxel-wise results (figures and tables) with specified thresholds and cluster sizes. Sample sizes meet the minimum (≥6) in patient and control groups. Full-text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for imaging modality, diagnosis, sample size, and whole-brain voxelwise reporting.

The study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients including some behavioural-variant cases (I4), has sufficient sample sizes (37 FTD patients; I5), and presents group-level voxelwise analyses described in the text (I7). However, the provided full text does not include explicit between-group results reported in a standard stereotactic coordinate space (MNI or Talairach), and I cannot verify any reported coordinates for voxelwise contrasts (criterion I6). Because I6 is required and cannot be confirmed from the provided full text, the study must be excluded. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses on a sample of clinically diagnosed behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) patients (n=23) and healthy controls (n=20). It includes whole-brain, voxelwise two-sample t-test group comparisons and voxelwise regression analyses confined to the patient group, with results described and displayed (figures/tables/supplementary). Sample sizes exceed the minimum threshold. Imaging modality (VBM on structural MRI) matches the inclusion imaging types. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only results, prohibited modalities, or comorbid-sample issues) are violated. Therefore the paper meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

The study used volumetric MRI segmentation (regional GM/WM volumes) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails inclusion I3). It reports lobar/regional volumetry and group comparisons, not whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinates in MNI/Talairach space (fails I6 and I7). The sample includes FTD and semantic dementia but does not explicitly state behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) diagnosis (fails I4). Therefore it does not meet the required imaging modality nor the whole-brain coordinate-based results required by the review. Full text appears complete.

While this study meets several methodological inclusion criteria (uses voxel-based morphometry; adequate sample sizes; reports whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts), it does not clearly report that the symptomatic patient sample consists of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) cases. Participants are described as genetic mutation carriers with progressive cognitive or behavioral change but the paper does not specify bvFTD diagnostic classification or apply accepted bvFTD clinical criteria. The review requires studies including clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4). Because I4 is not satisfied based on the provided full text, the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=24) (I4) with sample sizes above the minimum (I5); reports between-group voxelwise contrasts with MNI coordinates (e.g., 6, −46, 24) (I6); provides whole-brain, group-level VBM results (comparisons vs. controls and AD) that are clearly described (I7); and results/coordinates are reported in text/figures consistent with acceptable reporting (I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria are violated.

The full text reports an empirical study of clinically diagnosed frontal-variant (behavioral variant) FTD patients (n=13) using resting-state FDG-PET with voxelwise SPM2 analyses. Whole-brain, voxelwise cognitivo-metabolic correlations are reported with Talairach/MNI coordinates and cluster results (reported in text/figures/tables). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (patients and controls), and the paper includes complete methods, results, and discussion. Imaging modality, sample, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and coordinate reporting satisfy the review’s imaging and reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, reviews, disallowed modalities, comorbid psychiatric/neurological illness) are violated. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although the study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) methods (SPM12) and includes clinically diagnosed FTD cases (stated to correspond to bvFTD) with adequate sample sizes, it does not report a group-level, whole-brain between-group contrast (bvFTD group vs. controls) in a defined stereotactic space with reported coordinates. The paper focuses on single-subject VBM comparisons to a normative database to generate normative brain volume reports and presents SPM overlays/illustrations rather than group-level voxelwise results or coordinate tables in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7 required by the review.

This study includes a voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analysis (registered to MNI space) that corroborates the visual rating results. The sample contains clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=22) and healthy controls, satisfying sample-size requirements (≥6). Group-level voxelwise comparisons were performed and results are reported (with VBM results referenced in supplementary figures available online). Thus the paper provides whole-brain, between-group VBM findings for the target sample. Although peak coordinates are not shown in the main text, the authors state VBM analyses were registered to MNI space and supplementary VBM figures/tables are provided online, satisfying reporting requirements.

While the study uses FDG-PET and MRI (meets I3) and includes a sufficient number of FTLD patients (14; meets I5), it does not report that the patient sample specifically consists of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD). Participants are described generically as FTLD patients diagnosed by Neary criteria, with no breakdown by clinical subtype (bvFTD vs. semantic or language variants). The review requires inclusion of studies with clinically diagnosed bvFTD (I4), which is not satisfied here. Full text is complete and whole-brain voxelwise SVM maps are reported, but absence of explicit bvFTD diagnosis prevents inclusion.

Although this empirical study uses resting-state fMRI (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (81 bvFTD; I4) with adequate sample size (I5), it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The paper explicitly states no healthy control group was available and presents dynamic connectivity/metastate metrics derived from ICA components and state-space analyses rather than voxelwise whole-brain group-level contrasts or coordinate tables. Therefore it fails the requirement for reporting at least one between-group voxelwise result in stereotactic coordinates and lacks whole-brain voxelwise group-level results from the target sample, so it must be excluded.

This study does not include behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) patients. The sample comprises normal controls, Alzheimer’s disease, and semantic-variant PPA (SV-PPA) patients; VBM analyses were performed on NC and AD groups and explicitly excluded SV-PPA from the main VBM to avoid confounding. Although the study uses VBM (I3) and reports whole-brain results in MNI space (I6) and includes subgroup sizes ≥6 (SV-PPA n=10, meeting I5), it fails to meet the critical inclusion criterion I4 (study must include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients). Therefore it does not address the review objective (bvFTD) and must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a descriptive case series of five FTD-related gene carriers. Although individual patients had MRI and in one case FDG-PET, the study does not present group-level VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET analyses, provides no between-group contrasts or coordinates in MNI/Talairach space, and reports only 5 participants (fewer than the required minimum of 6). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I5 (sample size), I6 (between-group coordinate results), and I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group results). The full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a single-case clinical case report (n=1) of C9ORF72-associated slowly progressive FTLD presenting predominantly as semantic variant PPA. While FDG-PET was used (satisfying imaging modality criterion I3), the study does not include clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD patients (I4 not met), has far fewer than the required sample size (I5 not met), and it does not report any group-level between-group contrasts or whole-brain voxelwise results in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) (I6/I7 not met). Therefore it cannot contribute eligible whole-brain group-level coordinates or contrasts for the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete for the case report. Exclusion is based primarily on lack of whole-brain, group-level data and insufficient sample size.

The study uses resting-state fMRI (meets I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (18 bvFTD cases; meets I4), and has adequate sample sizes (32 FTD patients, 17 asymptomatic carriers; meets I5). It reports voxelwise, whole-brain results with stereotactic coordinates (e.g., -40,44,14) and cluster-level FWE-corrected findings in standard space (meets I6 and I7). Results are presented as coordinates and described in the text/figures (meets I8). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., review, ROI-only, seed-only FC, DTI-only, or non-empirical paper) are triggered. Therefore the paper satisfies all required inclusion criteria for this review.

The study uses voxelwise gray-matter MRI analyses consistent with VBM (meets I3) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group atrophy maps (meets I7/I8). However, it does not clearly specify inclusion of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) patients — participants are described as an FTD-spectrum clinical diagnosis without explicit labeling of bvFTD (I4 not clearly met). Critically, the VBM/imaging subgroup sample sizes for patient subgroups are very small (tau-positive n=5; tau-negative n=4; fv-AD n=3), so the target patient groups reported in whole-brain contrasts have <6 participants (fails I5). Coordinates in Table 3 are referenced but not shown in the provided text, making I6 uncertain. Because the key inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not satisfied (and I6 uncertain), the study is excluded from the bvFTD meta-analysis.

This study uses VBM (I3), has adequate sample sizes (30 per group; I5), and performs voxelwise analyses in MNI space with whole-brain voxelwise maps (I6, I7). However, the sample is described as “frontotemporal dementia (FTD)” without specification that patients are clinically-diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD). Inclusion criterion I4 requires that the study include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; this is not confirmed in the full text. Because I4 is not met, the study cannot be included for a review restricted to bvFTD. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

While the study meets several methodological inclusion criteria (uses VBM, reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level results in MNI space, and has sufficient sample sizes within patient groups), it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts (e.g., patient vs healthy control) in MNI/Talairach space. The analyses are within-group voxelwise correlations between neuropsychiatric symptom scores and grey-matter density across genetic FTD carriers, rather than between-group contrasts required by inclusion criterion I6. In addition, although symptomatic carriers are included (some meeting consensus criteria for bvFTD, PPA or FTD‑MND), the paper does not clearly present results specifically for a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (so I4 is not clearly satisfied). Therefore the study fails to meet key inclusion criteria (notably I6) and is excluded.

The study does NOT meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting inclusion criteria. It uses volumetric MRI measures (global whole-brain atrophy via BBSI and ventricular expansion via VBSI) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and it does not report any group-level voxelwise (MNI/Talairach) contrasts or coordinate tables of whole-brain analyses. Although bvFTD patients are included (n=11) and sample sizes meet the minimum, the absence of voxelwise whole-brain results and use of non-qualifying imaging modalities prevents inclusion in this review focused on VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET voxelwise studies. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study does not meet the imaging and analysis inclusion criteria. It uses conventional structural MRI descriptions (visual MRI findings) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not satisfied). It does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results nor provide coordinates in MNI/Talairach space (I6 and I7 not satisfied). Although bvFTD patients are included in the cohort, the imaging modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting required for this review are absent, so the study cannot be included.

This full-text reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses and diffusion tensor MRI in a cohort including 13 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and matched healthy controls. The paper presents whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts registered to MNI standard space (TBSS and VBM results are reported and visualized), and reports group-level results for bvFTD versus controls. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD N=13; controls N=25). The study therefore meets the imaging modality requirement (VBM), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants, reports whole-brain voxelwise results in a defined stereotaxic space, and presents those results in text/figures/tables. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, inappropriate imaging modality only) apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

Although the study uses VBM and FDG-PET (I3) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons with sufficient sample sizes (I5, I7, I8), the participant sample comprises patients with frontotemporal dementia plus motor neuron disease (FTD-MND). The meta-analysis exclusion criteria disallow samples with concurrent other neurological symptoms; inclusion of motor neuron disease therefore violates E4. Furthermore, the behavioral-dominant subgroup represents FTD-MND with behavioral features rather than a cohort of clinically diagnosed, isolated bvFTD patients. Because E4 is violated, the study must be excluded despite meeting several imaging and reporting criteria.

This is a single-case/family case report of corticobasal syndrome with PGRN mutation that includes FDG-PET images but does not study behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) patients. It does not meet key inclusion criteria: I4 (subjects are CBS/FTLD-U, not clinically diagnosed bvFTD), I5 (sample size is one proband / family — far fewer than 6), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space), and I7 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results). The paper is an empirical neuropathologic/genetic case report with neuroimaging but lacks the required group-based voxelwise analyses and bvFTD patient sample for meta-analysis. Therefore it must be excluded.

This is a case report of two siblings (n=2) with C9ORF72-associated FTD/ALS investigated with FDG- and 11C-PiB-PET. Although FDG-PET was used (I3), the study does not include clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD participants specified as bvFTD (I4 not clearly met), has an insufficient sample size (fails I5: only 2 patients), and provides no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts or coordinate-based results in MNI/Talairach space (fails I6 and I7). Therefore it does not meet the required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete. No predefined exclusion criteria (E2–E6) specifically apply, so exclusion is based on unmet inclusion criteria.

The full text reports both task-based fMRI (in healthy subjects) and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses including a direct, whole-brain VBM comparison between AD and bvFTD patients. Clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients were included (VBM sample n=48; behavioral samples include 14 and 15 bvFTD participants), satisfying minimum sample-size requirements. The paper provides group-level, voxelwise between-group contrasts with reported anatomical localization and MNI coordinates/figures and describes whole-brain results (significant GM density differences in prefrontal regions for bvFTD and medial temporal/parietal regions for AD). The text includes methods, results, and figures/tables supporting voxelwise findings. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for imaging modality (I3: VBM/fMRI), bvFTD sample (I4), sample size (I5), reporting of between-group contrasts in stochastic space (I6), whole-brain group-level voxelwise results (I7), and allows coordinate reporting in text/figures (I8).

The study does not meet the imaging and whole-brain analysis inclusion criteria. It uses structural MRI measures (a novel FA index and frontal atrophy ratios) rather than VBM, resting/task fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). The sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients but does not specify behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) specifically (I4 not met). The paper does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in MNI/Talairach space or coordinate tables/figures (I6 and I7 not met). Sample size criterion is met (41 FTDs) but failure to satisfy the imaging modality and voxelwise reporting criteria requires exclusion. Full text appears complete.

Although the study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients with behavioral-variant cases (I4) and the FTD group size is ≥6 (likely n=9; I5), it does not present any voxelwise, whole-brain group-level statistical contrasts in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The analysis is based on visual reading/classification of individual scans and reports concordance/sensitivity/specificity, without reporting coordinates, voxelwise maps, or whole-brain statistical results. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (and I8) requiring between-group voxelwise results in defined stochastic space. This matches exclusion criterion E3 (no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses (using DARTEL/SPM) and presents group-level voxelwise contrasts with MNI coordinates. The sample includes clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD patients (final diagnosis bvFTD in 12/19 C9ORF72 cases; 11 mutation carriers underwent volumetric MRI), meeting the minimum group size (n=11 patients, n=15 controls). Whole-brain, group-level VBM results are clearly reported for the C9ORF72 mutation group (overlaid on the MNI152 template and with MNI co-ordinates displayed in figures), and results are described in the text and figures. Although the imaging group is a genetic (C9ORF72) subgroup rather than an exclusively clinically-defined bvFTD group, the cohort includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases and the voxelwise whole-brain findings are applicable to bvFTD-related pathology reported in the manuscript. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria.

The full text reports an optimized voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analysis (meets I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (13 bvFTD; meets I4) and adequate group sizes (n>=6; meets I5). Voxel-wise between-group contrasts were performed after normalization to MNI space and whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps are reported and described (meets I6 and I7). Whole-brain results are presented in figures and described in text (meets I8). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria are violated.

This study is an audit of routine MRI reports and qualitative visual rating; it does not use VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET, nor does it report any group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or stereotactic coordinates. Although the sample includes 22 patients with FTD (meeting the minimum sample size), key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I3, I6, I7) are not met. Full text appears complete.

This article is a narrative review/author manuscript (Annual Review chapter) synthesizing evidence rather than reporting original empirical imaging data on bvFTD. It does not present a primary sample of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with an imaging study using VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, nor does it report between-group voxelwise coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails to meet multiple required inclusion criteria (I3–I7). It matches exclusion criteria for being a non-empirical review/meta-analytic paper (E2) and a non-empirical paper without original data (E5). Full text appears complete (introduction, discussion, references present).

This is an empirical neuroimaging study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=33) and matched healthy controls. Methods include voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and resting-state fMRI analyses with images normalized to MNI space; group-level, whole-brain voxelwise two-sample t-tests are reported and coordinates are provided (Supplementary Table 1). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD n=33; controls n=34). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts clearly attributed to the bvFTD group and presents results in figures/tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not DTI-only/seed-only, and patients without major comorbid psychiatric/neurological diagnoses). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This article is a scientific commentary (non-empirical) summarizing and discussing the findings of Jiskoot et al.; it does not present original empirical data or report primary whole-brain voxelwise results with stereotactic coordinates. It does not itself use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET to report between-group contrasts nor report a sample of clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants meeting the sample-size threshold. Therefore it fails to meet the review’s inclusion criteria and meets the exclusion criterion for non-empirical papers.

The full text reports an empirical, whole-brain voxelwise longitudinal morphometric analysis (SPM12/DARTEL; Jacobian determinant contraction maps) comparing bvFTD patients to healthy controls. The study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (n=44) and HCs (n=97), exceeding the minimum sample size. Analyses are performed in standardized (MNI) space with group-level t-maps, consensus ROIs, and cross-validated effect sizes—i.e., between-group voxelwise contrasts are reported and displayed. The manuscript contains full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. Therefore it meets the imaging modality requirement (voxel-based morphometry-style voxelwise analysis), includes bvFTD patients, reports whole-brain voxelwise results in MNI space, and provides sufficient data for inclusion.

The study does not meet key inclusion criteria for this review. It uses tau and amyloid PET imaging ([11C]PBB3 and [11C]PiB), not one of the required modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) (I3 unmet). The sample comprises 10 patients with familial FTDP-17 due to MAPT N279K mutation (a genetic frontotemporal dementia with parkinsonism), but patients are not characterized as clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) as required (I4 unmet); most cases are PSP-like and only two had initial personality changes.
